props.title: The Criminal
props.initialSlug: Ex-con plans perfect bank heist with deadly twist

sections.content: **The Criminal** (1960) stands as Joseph Losey's stark British noir masterpiece, crafted during his blacklist exile from Hollywood. The film revolutionized British crime cinema with its brutal realism and complex character study of ex-con Johnny Bannion (Stanley Baker). It shares DNA with other prison-break classics like **Escape from Alcatraz** (1979) and **A Man Escaped** (1956), but Losey's psychological approach digs deeper into criminal psychology than his contemporaries dared.

sections.content: Losey's direction shows clear influence from film noir but pushes beyond genre conventions. Like **Kiss Me Deadly** (1955) and **Touch of Evil** (1958), The Criminal employs expressionistic angles and shadows while exploring moral ambiguity. The prison sequences, shot at Blackbushe Prison, set a new standard for realism that influenced everything from **Cool Hand Luke** (1967) to **The Shawshank Redemption** (1994).

The film's treatment of criminality broke new ground in British cinema. Unlike the polite crime films of the 1950s, Losey portrays the underworld with unflinching brutality. Stanley Baker's performance as Johnny Bannion influenced a generation of British tough-guy actors, from Michael Caine in Get Carter (1971) to Bob Hoskins in **The Long Good Friday** (1980). sections.content: The Criminal's prison sequences established new conventions for the genre. The film's documentary-style approach to institutional life influenced **Scum** (1979) and **McVicar** (1980). Johnny Bannion's psychological deterioration in solitary confinement provides a template followed by films like **Bronson** (2008) and **In the Name of the Father** (1993).

The film's innovative jazz score by Johnny Dankworth complements Losey's visual style while establishing a new sound for British crime cinema. This musical approach influenced scores from Get Carter (1971) to **The Long Good Friday** (1980), helping define the sonic landscape of British gangster films.
